newsitem.title: USA: US House tax plan offers no change on cap gains.
newsitem.headline: US House tax plan offers no change on cap gains.

text.p: The first offer from U.S. House tax conferees to the Senate does not include any changes in the capital gains and ethanol provisions that were in the House bill, a House Republican aide said.
House and Senate tax conferees are trying to work out differences in their separate bills so that Congress can vote on a single final tax cut bill.

The House's first offer also did not include a cigarette tax increase, which is in the Senate bill, the aide said. The Senate legislation would raise about $15 billion from a 20 cents per pack cigarette tax increase.
The House bill includes "indexing" for capital gains which would allow taking into account the effects of inflation when calculating the tax on profits made on certain investments.
The White House has strongly opposed that provision and the Senate bill does not include it.
The House bill also would end the ethanol subsidy after it expired at the end of 2000, while the Senate bill would retain the subsidy but gradually reduce it in 2001 to 2007.
The major issues in the tax bills are unlikely to be addressed until later in the process.
